title: F1: Cargo workspace skeleton + hid link layer + JSON output
description: Create the Rust CLI skeleton for `omg`. Deps: clap(derive), anyhow, thiserror, hidapi=2.6, serde, serde_json. Port the Link trait + HidLink + transfer() from ../oh-my-gravastar-upstream/orbit-gravastar/src/hid.rs (85 lines, MIT). Global flags: --json (serde_json output for every command), --device <path|vid:pid> (auto-select when exactly one match), exit codes 0 ok / 1 error / 2 no-device / 3 unsupported. Implement `omg devices` that enumerates hidapi device_list and reports any device matching known GravaStar identities: keyboard v2 (VID 1CA6/31E3, usage 0xFFB0), SparkPlayJoy (usage 0xFFA0), mouse Compx (VID 3554 PIDs F54B F575 F548 F577 F576 F549, usage 0xFF02), khub916 wired (VID 258A PID 010C and table in docs/plan.md) + 916_wireLess table. Output must include vid, pid, product string, usage page, path. Unit test: mock device list. This is the foundation every other bead builds on.

title: F12a: Protocol codec unit tests + CI workflow
description: Port packet-level unit tests from orbit-gravastar (mouse.rs tests: packet checksum bytes, DPI encode/decode roundtrip, battery voltage curve). Add decode fuzz tests for all protocol parsers (proptest or quickcheck). GitHub Actions CI: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test on ubuntu/macos/windows matrix. Every protocol module must have tests before its CLI bead closes.

title: F5a: Reverse khub916 HID engine from vendor JS
description: Main research task. Deobfuscate docs/research/khub-webapp/index-M8-m9qFR.js (207KB, string-table obfuscation s(NNN) lookups, sendFeatureReport queue). Goals: (1) HID device selection criteria (collections with outputReports>0 && featureReports>0), (2) report ID used, (3) packet envelope format (header, length, checksum, sequence), (4) auth/password handshake using per-model password (K1 = 0x0300000001b4, protocolKey 916), (5) command IDs for: device info, layout/keymap read, lighting get/set, key remap, macro, profile. Cross-reference chunk files (devicesInit, home, screensInit, BasicFunctions, LightingEffect, MacroConfiguration, AdvancedKey, ConfigurationManagement) for call sites. Document findings in docs/protocol-khub916.md BEFORE writing Rust code. Verify read-only commands against the live K1 Pro (VID 258A PID 010C, currently connected via USB cable). Safety: until a command is proven read-only, do not send it from Rust; probe via a scratch script only.

title: F5b: Implement khub916 protocol module in Rust
description: Depends on F5a + F1. Implement src/proto/khub916.rs per docs/protocol-khub916.md: device matching (VID/PID tables incl. wireless), feature-report transport via Link, auth handshake, typed commands for info/layout/keys/lighting read paths first, then writes behind validation. Port semantics from the JS reference, not byte-for-byte guesses. Include captured-packet fixtures from the live K1 Pro in tests/.

title: F5c: khub916 CLI commands (K1/K98 series)
description: Depends on F5b. CLI: omg kb916 info|layout|keys|get|set for protocol-916 devices. Reads first (info, layout/keymap, lighting state); writes require --yes + read-back verify. Key naming: use HID usage -> label table ported from orbit models.rs key_label (EN first; DE optional). Layout comes from device if protocol provides geometry, else fall back to a K1 Pro ANSI layout table in model/. Must work against live K1 Pro on macOS.

title: F2: Port HE v2 keyboard protocol to Rust
description: Port ../oh-my-gravastar-upstream/orbit-gravastar/src/protocol/keyboard.rs (365 lines) + needed parts of models.rs (key_size, key_label, lighting zone tables). Keep protocol/blacklist separation: this module exposes only safe categories (1,2,3,4,5 reads+writes); firmware update (8), custom wipe (10 01 01 FF), tri-mode gamepad (10 02), categories C/E/F are NOT implemented. Document each command's safety class in code comments. Unit tests: packet build/parse fixtures.

title: F3: HE keyboard CLI commands
description: Depends on F2 + F1. omg kb <cmd>: info, layout (geometry+keycodes->labels), profile get/set, polling get/set (8K..125, warns keyboard restarts), os get/set, perf get/set <row> <col> (mode fixed|rt, actuation mm, RT params, deadzones — validate <= switch max travel from axis_v2_id; UFO 13232 => 3.5mm else 3.4mm), light get/set <area> + palette, calibration start|stop (documented as device operation, requires --yes), live <row> travel readout. Writes: --yes flag + read-back verify + JSON verified field. factory-reset deliberately NOT exposed.

title: F4: Port Compx mouse protocol + CLI
description: Port orbit-gravastar/src/protocol/mouse.rs (476 lines, has unit tests) + mouse protocol doc. omg mouse: info (identify cid/mid/model/sensor/link), battery, firmware, config (full flash map decode: polling, DPI stages+colors, LOD, buttons, lighting, debounce, motion sync, sleep, angle snap, ripple, sensor mode), set subcommands for each with --yes + read-back verify. Enforce WRITABLE flash allowlist; never implement pairing(05/06), factory reset(09), RF channel(31), bootloader B0-B7. DPI encode/decode + battery voltage table ported with tests. Wireless dongle may be asleep: implement wake/poll like OmaGravastar wake_and_battery.py.

title: F6: SparkPlayJoy 6x21 analog travel reader
description: Depends on F2. Implement framed protocol 5C <len> <cmd> <cksum> <payload> on usage 0xFFA0:0001 per HallJoy docs (GRAVASTAR_MERCURY_V75_FIRMWARE_STATIC_ANALYSIS_2026-08-22.md) and aula_win60he_protocol.{h,cpp} reference. Read-only commands only: sync 01, scale order 0x25, default map 0x2B, active map 0x23, live travel 0x12 (two halves -> 63 u16 each, 6x21 matrix, ~5um). Output: omg kb travel-matrix --json stream or snapshot. Identity gate: only exact GravaStar board IDs (16052201/16052202/2E022201) auto-claim; unknown 6x21 devices get structural proof only, never guessed. Needs HE keyboard to verify — document as pending-hardware if unavailable.

title: F7: Unified profile export/import (JSON schema v1)
description: Depends on F3 + F4. omg profile export <file.json> / import <file.json>: capture all readable settings per device (kb v2 + khub916 + mouse) into one versioned JSON document {schema:1, device:{vid,pid,model}, profiles:[...]}. Import validates schema + device match, backs up current state first (like OmaGravastar), writes via verified path. Include --dry-run. Mouse web-driver .bin compat is a later optional extra, not required.

title: F8: omg probe raw diagnostic command
description: Like orbit --probe: for each connected GravaStar device, dump identity, all readable state, and raw hex of key replies. Essential for adding new models safely (the 916 device table will grow). Read-only; never sends unproven writes. Output text + --json.

title: F11: macOS HID permissions + platform docs
description: Document macOS specifics: hidapi uses IOHIDManager; first access may need user approval in System Settings > Privacy > Input Monitoring (or the app prompts). Add docs/platforms.md covering macOS/Linux(hidraw udev rules like OmaGravastar)/Windows. Test omg devices on macOS with the K1 Pro.

title: F9: ratatui TUI dashboard (phase 2)
description: Optional human UI over the same proto layer: device list, battery/status, keyboard layout view with live travel (once F6 lands), lighting controls. Depends on F3+F4 cores being stable. Low priority — CLI is the product.

title: F10: Offline web UI / PWA via WebHID (phase 3)
description: Only if demanded. WebHID version of the same protocol layer (mouse-protocol proves TS/WebHID works for Compx; khub916 already IS WebHID so K1 support is natural in browser). Reuse proto logic ported to TS or wasm. Defer until CLI mature.

title: Docs: README + AGENTS.md + protocol docs
description: README: what it is, install (cargo install / brew later), quickstart omg devices + omg kb info, feature matrix per device family, safety rules, non-affiliation disclaimer (GravaStar/Mercury trademarks). AGENTS.md: safety contract from docs/plan.md section 2, test commands, bead workflow pointer. docs/protocol-*.md: consolidate upstream protocol docs (khub916, HE v2, SparkPlayJoy, Compx) with provenance links.
